title: Roman Numerals: Reading, Writing and Converting
seo_title: Roman Numerals – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Read and write Roman numerals up to M (1,000) and beyond; convert between Roman numerals and Hindu-Arabic numerals; add and subtract numbers written in Roman numerals. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on Roman numerals: the symbols I, V, X, L, C, D and M, reading and writing numbers up to 3,000, converting and simple sums. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Big to small: add. Small before big: subtract.
key_sub: IV 4, IX 9, XL 40, XC 90, CD 400, CM 900
body_html:
How to think about it

  • I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1,000.
  • Write the thousands, then the hundreds, tens and units: 1,846 = M + DCCC + XL + VI = MDCCCXLVI.
  • Only I, X and C go in front of a bigger symbol to subtract, and never more than one.

Examples

Example

Write 949

900 = CM, 40 = XL, 9 = IX

Answer: CMXLIX

Example

MCCXV

1,000 + 200 + 10 + 5

Answer: 1,215

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing IC for 9999 = 90 + 9 = XCIX.
Repeating a symbol four times4 is IV, not IIII; 40 is XL, not XXXX.
Adding a small symbol in frontIn IX the I is taken away: 10 − 1 = 9.

faq.q: Is there a Roman numeral for zero?
faq.a: No. The Romans had no symbol for zero.

faq.q: Where do we see Roman numerals?
faq.a: On clocks, in book chapters, and in the names of kings such as Elizabeth II.

items.q: What number does C stand for?
items.e: C = 100. C is the first letter of centum, the Latin word for a hundred (think of a century). L is 50 and D is 500.

items.q: What number does D stand for?
items.e: D = 500. Do not mix it up with L (50) or M (1,000).

items.q: What number does M stand for?
items.e: M = 1,000. It comes from mille, the Latin word for a thousand. M does not stand for a million.

items.q: What number does L stand for?
items.e: L = 50. D is 500, C is 100 and V is 5.

items.q: Which Roman numeral means 500?
items.e: 500 has its own symbol: D. DM is not allowed: D is never put before a bigger symbol. CCCCC uses 5 Cs, but you never write more than 3 of the same symbol in a row. M is 1,000.

items.q: Which Roman numeral means 1,000?
items.e: 1,000 has its own symbol: M. DD is not allowed: D is never repeated. D is 500 and CM is 900.

items.q: Which Roman numeral means 100?
items.e: C = 100. L is 50, D is 500 and XC is 90.

items.q: Which three symbols are never repeated, like VV or DD?
items.e: V, L and D are never repeated, because two of them make another symbol: VV = X, LL = C and DD = M.

items.q: Which symbols can go in front of a bigger symbol to be taken away?
items.e: Only I, X and C are taken away: IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM. V, L and D are never put before a bigger symbol.

items.q: What is the most times you can write the same symbol in a row?
items.e: Never more than 3 in a row: III = 3, XXX = 30, CCC = 300. 4 is IV, 40 is XL and 400 is CD.

items.q: What number is XIV?
items.e: Split it: X = 10; IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So XIV = 10 + 4 = 14. The I is before the V, so take it away: XIV is not 16.

items.q: What number is XXXIX?
items.e: Split it: XXX = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XXXIX = 30 + 9 = 39. IX is 9, not 11, so XXXIX is not 41.

items.q: What number is XLIX?
items.e: Split it: XL = 50 − 10 = 40; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XLIX = 40 + 9 = 49. Adding every symbol gives 71, which is wrong.

items.q: What number is LXXXVIII?
items.e: Split it: LXXX = 50 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 80; VIII = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8. So LXXXVIII = 80 + 8 = 88. Count carefully: L and three Xs make 80, then VIII is 8.

items.q: What number is XCIV?
items.e: Split it: XC = 100 − 10 = 90; IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So XCIV = 90 + 4 = 94. XC is 90, not 110, and IV is 4, not 6.

items.q: What number does I stand for?
items.e: I means 1.

items.q: What number does V stand for?
items.e: V means 5. Do not mix it up with X, which means 10.

items.q: What number does X stand for?
items.e: X means 10.

items.q: Which Roman numeral stands for 50?
Which Roman numeral means 5?
items.e: 5 has its own symbol: V. VX is not a Roman numeral: V is never put before a bigger symbol. IIIII uses 5 Is, but you never write more than 3 of the same symbol in a row.

items.q: What number is CCC?
items.e: CCC = 100 + 100 + 100 = 300. Each C is 100. Do not mix C up with X (10).

items.q: What number is DC?
items.e: DC = 500 + 100 = 600. The smaller C comes after the D, so add it. D is 500, not 1,000 (M) or 50 (L).

items.q: What number is CD?
items.e: CD = 500 − 100 = 400. The smaller C comes before the D, so take it away: CD is not 600.

items.q: What number is CM?
items.e: CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900. The C comes before the M, so take it away: CM is not 1,100.

items.q: What number is DCCC?
items.e: DCCC = 500 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 800. Count the Cs: there are three. D is 500, not 1,000.

items.q: What number is CXX?
items.e: Split it: C = 100; XX = 10 + 10 = 20. So CXX = 100 + 20 = 120. The Xs come after the C, so add them. Roman numerals have no place value, so it is not 102.

items.q: What number is CCLX?
items.e: Split it: CC = 100 + 100 = 200; LX = 50 + 10 = 60. So CCLX = 200 + 60 = 260. LX is 60. XL would be 40.

items.q: What number is CDL?
items.e: Split it: CD = 500 − 100 = 400; L = 50. So CDL = 400 + 50 = 450. CD is 400, not 600, so CDL is not 650.

items.q: What number is DXL?
What number is CCXLV?
What number is CDIX?
items.e: Split it: CD = 500 − 100 = 400; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So CDIX = 400 + 9 = 409. CD is 400 and IX is 9: take away both times.

items.q: What number is CMIV?
items.e: Split it: CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900; IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So CMIV = 900 + 4 = 904. CM is 900 and IV is 4: take away both times.

items.q: What number is CXLIX?
items.e: Split it: C = 100; XL = 50 − 10 = 40; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So CXLIX = 100 + 40 + 9 = 149. XL is 40, not 60, and IX is 9, not 11.

items.q: What number is DCLXVI?
items.e: Split it: DC = 500 + 100 = 600; LX = 50 + 10 = 60; VI = 5 + 1 = 6. So DCLXVI = 600 + 60 + 6 = 666. Every symbol here is followed by a smaller one, so add them all. DCLXVI uses D, C, L, X, V and I once each.

items.q: What number is DCCLXXVII?
items.e: Split it: DCC = 500 + 100 + 100 = 700; LXX = 50 + 10 + 10 = 70; VII = 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. So DCCLXXVII = 700 + 70 + 7 = 777. Count carefully: DCC = 700, LXX = 70, VII = 7.

items.q: What number is CCCXCIX?
What number is CDXCIV?
items.e: Split it: CD = 500 − 100 = 400; XC = 100 − 10 = 90; IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So CDXCIV = 400 + 90 + 4 = 494. CD is 400 (not 600), XC is 90 (not 110) and IV is 4 (not 6).

items.q: What number is DCCCLXXXVIII?
items.e: Split it: DCCC = 500 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 800; LXXX = 50 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 80; VIII = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8. So DCCCLXXXVIII = 800 + 80 + 8 = 888. Count carefully: three Cs, three Xs and three Is.

items.q: What number is CMXC?
What number is CMXCIX?
items.e: Split it: CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900; XC = 100 − 10 = 90; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So CMXCIX = 900 + 90 + 9 = 999. 999 is the biggest number below 1,000. It is never written IM.

items.q: Which symbols are missing? 760 = DCC ?
items.e: 760 = 700 + 60. DCC = 700, so the missing part is 60 = LX.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: CCCC is not correct: 400 is written CD. The others are correct: CD = 400, DC = 600, CM = 900.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: XD is not correct: X can only go before L or C, so 490 = CD + XC = CDXC. The others are correct: CDXC = 490, CMXL = 940, DXC = 590.

items.q: Which symbols are missing? 940 = CM ?
items.e: 940 = 900 + 40. CM = 900, so the missing part is 40 = XL.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: DD is not correct: D is never repeated, so 1,000 is written M. The others are correct: M = 1,000, CC = 200, CCC = 300.

items.q: Write the number 6 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 6 into 6: VI.

items.q: Write the number 69 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 69 into 60 + 9: LXIX.

items.q: Write the number 456 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 456 into 400 + 50 + 6: CDLVI.

items.q: Write the number 20 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 20 into 20: XX.

items.q: Write the number 131 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 131 into 100 + 30 + 1: CXXXI.

items.q: Write the number 504 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 504 into 500 + 4: DIV.

items.q: Write the number 10 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 10 into 10: X.

items.q: Write the number 44 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 44 into 40 + 4: XLIV.

items.q: Write the number 922 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 922 into 900 + 20 + 2: CMXXII.

items.q: Write the number 779 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 779 into 700 + 70 + 9: DCCLXXIX.

items.q: Write the number 31 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 31 into 30 + 1: XXXI.

items.q: Write the number 32 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 32 into 30 + 2: XXXII.

items.q: Write the number 111 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 111 into 100 + 10 + 1: CXI.

items.q: Write the number 956 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 956 into 900 + 50 + 6: CMLVI.

items.q: Write the number 977 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 977 into 900 + 70 + 7: CMLXXVII.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: XL = 40 and LX = 60. 40 < 60, so XL < LX.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: XXIX = 29, XXXV = 35, XXXVIII = 38, XL = 40. XL is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the smallest?
items.e: VIII = 8, IX = 9, XI = 11, XII = 12. VIII is the smallest.

items.q: What comes next? XXXVI, XXXVII, XXXVIII, ?
items.e: XXXVI = 36, XXXVII = 37, XXXVIII = 38. The numbers go up in 1s. 38 + 1 = 39 = XXXIX.

items.q: What comes next? XL, L, LX, ?
items.e: XL = 40, L = 50, LX = 60. The numbers go up in 10s. 60 + 10 = 70 = LXX.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
items.e: XVI = 16, XIX = 19, XXI = 21. From smallest to largest: XVI, XIX, XXI.

items.q: Work out XXIV + VI. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XXIV = 24 and VI = 6. 24 + 6 = 30, and 30 = XXX.

items.q: Work out XV + IX. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XV = 15 and IX = 9. 15 + 9 = 24, and 24 = XXIV.

items.q: Work out XL + X. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out XXXV + XV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out L − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: L = 50 and I = 1. 50 − 1 = 49, and 49 = XLIX. IL is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.

items.q: Work out XC − X. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out XIX + XXI. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XIX = 19 and XXI = 21. 19 + 21 = 40, and 40 = XL. XXXX is wrong: never write 4 Xs in a row.

items.q: Work out LX − XV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: LX = 60 and XV = 15. 60 − 15 = 45, and 45 = XLV. VL is not allowed: only I, X (and C) go before a bigger symbol, and only I before V or X.

items.q: Work out XLV + XLV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XLV = 45 and XLV = 45. 45 + 45 = 90, and 90 = XC. LXXXX is wrong: never write 4 Xs in a row.

items.q: Work out C − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: C = 100 and I = 1. 100 − 1 = 99, and 99 = XCIX. IC is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: IX = 9 and XI = 11. 9 < 11, so IX < XI.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: XL = 40, XLVIII = 48, LIV = 54, LX = 60. LX is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: LXXIX = 79, LXXXV = 85, LXXXVIII = 88, XC = 90. XC is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
items.e: XXXV = 35, XL = 40, L = 50. From smallest to largest: XXXV, XL, L.
The minute hand (red) points to III, which is quarter past. The hour hand has just passed X (10), so it is quarter past ten. Be careful: X is 10 and XI is 11.
The minute hand (red) points to IX, which is quarter to. The hour hand is nearly at IV (4), so it is quarter to four. Be careful: IV is 4, not 6.

items.q: At the end of a film, Dayo sees “© MCMXCVII”. In what year was the film made?
In what year was this stone laid?
Simi’s favourite film came out in MCMXCIX and its sequel in MMIX. How many years apart are they?
items.e: MCMXCIX = 1,999 and MMIX = 2,009. 2,009 − 1,999 = 10 years. Reading IX as 11 gives 12 or 8, and forgetting the first M of MCMXCIX gives 1,010.

items.q: M comes from mille, the Latin word for a thousand. Which English word also comes from mille?
items.e: A millennium is 1,000 years. Metre, minute and medium come from other Latin and Greek words.

items.q: Which list of years goes from earliest to latest?
items.e: MCMLX = 1,960, MCMLXX = 1,970, MCMXC = 1,990. From earliest to latest: MCMLX, MCMLXX, MCMXC.

items.q: Work out CM + C. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: CM = 900 and C = 100. 900 + 100 = 1,000, and 1,000 = M. CMC just puts the numerals side by side. DD is not allowed: D is never repeated.

items.q: Work out M − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: M = 1,000 and I = 1. 1,000 − 1 = 999, and 999 = CMXCIX. IM is not allowed: I can only go before V or X. MI is 1,001.

items.q: Work out D − CC. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: D = 500 and CC = 200. 500 − 200 = 300, and 300 = CCC. CCD is not a Roman numeral: only one C can go before D. DCC is 500 + 200.

items.q: Work out CDL + L. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: CDL = 450 and L = 50. 450 + 50 = 500, and 500 = D. CD is 400, not 600, so the answer is not DCC (700).

items.q: Work out C × V. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: C = 100 and V = 5. 100 × 5 = 500, and 500 = D. CV is 105, not 100 × 5. M is 100 × 10. CCCCC has too many Cs.

items.q: A foundation stone says MCMXXXVI. Ifeanyi reads it as 2,136. What mistake did he make?
c: Added the C instead of taking it away
items.e: MCMXXXVI = M + CM + XXX + VI = 1,000 + 900 + 30 + 6, so the year is 1,936. Adding the C gives 1,000 + 100 + 1,000 + 30 + 6 = 2,136. The C comes before the M, so it must be taken away.

items.q: Which year is not written correctly?
items.e: MIM is not correct: I can only go before V or X. 1,999 is written MCMXCIX. The others are correct: MCMXCIX = 1,999, MCMLXXX = 1,980, MMXX = 2,020.

items.q: At the end of a film, Amaka sees “© MCMXCVII”. In what year was the film made?
A foundation stone says MCMXXXVI. Yusuf reads it as 2,136. What mistake did he make?
c: Added the C instead of taking it away
items.e: MCMXXXVI = M + CM + XXX + VI = 1,000 + 900 + 30 + 6, so the year is 1,936. Adding the C gives 1,000 + 100 + 1,000 + 30 + 6 = 2,136. The C comes before the M, so it must be taken away.

items.q: At the end of a film, Tolu sees “© MCMXCVII”. In what year was the film made?
Ifeanyi’s favourite film came out in MCMXCIX and its sequel in MMIX. How many years apart are they?
items.e: MCMXCIX = 1,999 and MMIX = 2,009. 2,009 − 1,999 = 10 years. Reading IX as 11 gives 12 or 8, and forgetting the first M of MCMXCIX gives 1,010.

items.q: A foundation stone says MCMXXXVI. Ikenna reads it as 2,136. What mistake did he make?
c: Added the C instead of taking it away
items.e: MCMXXXVI = M + CM + XXX + VI = 1,000 + 900 + 30 + 6, so the year is 1,936. Adding the C gives 1,000 + 100 + 1,000 + 30 + 6 = 2,136. The C comes before the M, so it must be taken away.
